metadata.title: SoftBank Group shares surge 11% as Asian tech stocks rally after Wall Street rebounds

left: South Korea’s KOSPI rose 5.49% to 5,294.35 after gains on Wall Street and reduced uncertainty surrounding the Middle East.
The Korea Exchange suspended program trading for five minutes after the KOSPI’s sharp rise.
South Korean technology stocks advanced, with Samsung Electronics gaining 5.85% and SK hynix rising 8.63%.
U.S. markets rose while Nvidia fell 4.2% and oil prices declined.
center: On Tuesday, the Korea Composite Stock Price Index surged, prompting the Korea Exchange to activate a buy-side sidecar that suspended program trading for five minutes at 9:06 a.m.
Asian technology stocks surged Tuesday, tracking overnight Wall Street gains as eased military tensions in the Middle East lifted sentiment amid hopes for diplomatic talks ending the U.S.-Iran war.
Semiconductor shares led the rebound, with the PHLX semiconductor index jumping 6.85 percent. Market bellwether Samsung Electronics rose 5.85 percent, while chipmaker SK hynix soared 8.63 percent.
As of 9:10 a.m., the KOSPI added 240.01 points, or 4.78 percent, to 5,258.86. Defense giant Hanwha Aerospace rose 4.85 percent, and major banking group KB Financial Group increased 4.31 percent.

The rally followed last week's bruising sell-off, with renewed buying in chip names spilling over into Asia as falling oil prices calmed inflation fears. Sentiment across the region improved despite a scandal swirling around Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang.
